repo_evidence: The representative matrix covers 8 classes directly: Priest, Paladin, Rogue, Shaman, Warlock, Druid, Mage, and Demon Hunter. CuteWarrior adds Warrior as supplemental load-safe proof. Hunter and Death Knight are not represented, but the matrix goal is runtime-family breadth rather than class-complete ladder coverage.
The representative matrix includes 9 core source-backed rows: ShadowPriest, CtAPaladin, PirateRogue, BigShaman, Discolock, TreantDruid, ImbueMage, MechPala, and PirateDH.

The representative matrix includes 2 source-informed valid rows: Kingslayer and Boarlock. Both are intentionally retained because they expose hard source-confidence gaps while still proving technical load-safe package generation.

Boarlock is preserved with first_strongness_gap=needs_mulligan_claim_for_fracking and stop_condition=exact_boarlock_fracking_mulligan_source_unavailable. It is also the only representative Combo.json control row.

CuteWarrior is not counted as a twelfth representative row. Its proof role is supplemental_load_safe_only, and its known limits explicitly say it does not change representative matrix count or close the Kingslayer and Boarlock gaps.
The universal no-block matrix test makes the important operational promise executable across all 12 user-provided inputs instead of relying only on documentation.

The operator docs define GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json as the minimal load-safe runtime files, with per-card JSON as HSConfig rich-output repo policy and Combo.json emitted only when the deck and evidence support it.

The current mechanic support code and tests keep unsupported or unresolved mechanic semantics visible through reports, suppression, partial support, or warning-only buckets instead of inventing unsafe runtime rows.

no_block_assessment: Nothing is blocked can safely mean that a valid deck input can produce a structurally valid, load-safe initial package with GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json, and can be applied through load_safe_apply when the operator gate allows it.
Nothing is blocked must not mean that every deck is SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG, that every modern Wild mechanic is first-class lowerable, or that every source-confidence gap is closed.

The set is useful because it includes both clean source-backed rows and preserved source-informed rows. Kingslayer and Boarlock prove that source-depth debt remains visible while runtime load safety remains available.

The no-block proof is strongest at the package-shape level: exact deck identity, required runtime files, per-card rich output, optional Combo.json, warning-only mechanic visibility, and no normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json.

Source confidence, mechanic visibility, source-depth gaps, combo precision, and review-only warnings remain report surfaces. They should guide follow-up research but should not become runtime hard blocks for a technically valid package.

Technical hard blocks remain appropriate for malformed deckcodes, invalid JSON, unsupported runtime filenames or blocks, missing GlobalValues.json or Mulligan.json, undeclared runtime files, nested runtime files, normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json, and forged or stale apply evidence.
skill_slimness_assessment: The matrix is slim because it uses representative runtime families rather than trying to mirror every Wild ladder archetype.
Keeping CuteWarrior supplemental is the right size-control decision: it proves a narrow acceptance lane while leaving the representative matrix at 11 rows.
Keeping Boarlock and Kingslayer as source-informed controls is leaner and more honest than adding easier replacement decks that avoid the first missing source-depth chains.

The skill boundary remains clean because the evidence stays in pre-run HSConfig outputs and operator reports, not HSranger runtime tuning, HSTuner replay analysis, winrate analysis, or post-game candidate promotion.
The current design prefers warning-only and partial mechanic visibility over broad runtime-surface invention. That keeps the skill understandable and reduces future fixture maintenance.
Adding a new representative deck should require a proven uncovered runtime family or source-depth failure that none of the current 11 representative rows plus CuteWarrior can expose.

hearthstone_semantic_coverage.assessment: Adequate for a lean proof but not class-complete. The set covers Priest, Paladin, Rogue, Shaman, Warlock, Druid, Mage, Demon Hunter, and supplemental Warrior. Hunter and Death Knight are not represented, but the tested runtime families matter more than full class enumeration for HSConfig package safety.
Strong. ShadowPriest, PirateRogue, PirateDH, TreantDruid, and CuteWarrior cover proactive pressure from burn, weapons, hero attacks, board flood, and low-curve shells.
Strong. CtAPaladin, TreantDruid, MechPala, BigShaman, and Discolock cover board flood, aura pressure, token snowball, magnetic or mech scaling, recruit, deathrattle, and payoff summon patterns.

Adequate but intentionally narrow. Boarlock is the representative combo-control and Combo.json row. The set should not add more combo rows until a different combo package exposes a new compiler failure that Boarlock cannot reveal.
Strong. PirateRogue, Kingslayer, and PirateDH cover weapon pressure, long-form attack sequencing, and hero-attack pressure from different class and archetype angles.

Adequate. ShadowPriest covers hero-power transform, ImbueMage covers hero-power and imbue posture, and generated entity or spell generation remains partial or identity-gated where exact identities are unresolved.
Strong for the audit goal. The matrix intentionally keeps 9 source-backed-strong rows and 2 source-informed valid rows, proving both clean closure and warning-visible source debt.

Adequate for no-block visibility, not exhaustive first-class lowering. Mechanic support and drift tests cover direct, identity-gated-direct, partial, warning-only, unknown, and modern text-only mechanics without requiring a dedicated fixture for every keyword.

Secret-heavy timing, freeze-control, location-heavy reactive control, overload-first timing, discover-chain control, Hunter class shells, and Death Knight class shells are not primary representative rows today. This is acceptable for the lean proof unless one of those families demonstrates a real package-shape or runtime-surface gap.

gaps_or_risks: The set is representative, not exhaustive. It cannot prove every current or future Wild deck family, class, card package, or mechanic combination.
Hunter and Death Knight are not represented in the current 11-plus-1 user-provided set. That is a class-coverage gap, but not yet a proven HSConfig package-safety gap.

Secret-heavy timing, location-heavy control, overload-first shells, freeze-control, and discover-chain control are not isolated as primary rows. These should remain watch items rather than automatic fixture additions.
Kingslayer still lacks exact Kingslayer or Kingsbane Quick Pick mulligan evidence, so it must remain source-informed until that specific stop condition closes.
Boarlock still lacks exact Boarlock-relevant Fracking mulligan evidence and retains source-informed blockers, so it must remain source-informed until those exact gaps close.

The current no-block claim depends on the distinction between technical load safety and semantic confidence. If future docs or code blur that distinction, the matrix could appear stronger or weaker than it really is.
Future Hearthstone mechanics may drift beyond current static detection. The right response is first to add non-blocking visibility or warning rows, not to add a full representative deck by default.
Fixture bloat remains the main governance risk: adding more decks for popularity, class completion, or duplicate aggro and pirate pressure would increase maintenance cost without improving the proof.
recommended_next_action: Keep the representative matrix at 11 decks plus supplemental CuteWarrior, and add no new representative deck unless a future failing or audit proves a runtime-family or source-depth gap that the current set cannot expose.
confidence: high - the verdict is grounded in the current operator docs, matrix governance files, source-closure docs, mechanic visibility tests, supplemental CuteWarrior proof, and the universal 12-deck no-block test.
